To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

patients with advanced cancer who have a high level of symptom burden have a high level on at least one of the ESAS items and a low level of QOL, and that the most common symptom that contributes to high burden is pain, which is also the symptom that most commonly contributes to poor QOL.
patients with advanced cancer followed by palliative providers have a high self-defined symptom burden, and patients with any symptom rated ≥7 on the ESAS have a high self defined symptom burden.
Patients with advanced disease followed up by palliative care services are a group with high symptom burden, as defined by themselves.

the development of a patient-centred definition of symptom burden.

patients with a high level (7 or more) on any ESAS item have high symptom burden.

symptom burden is a multidimensional construct that can be measured using the Edmonton Symptom assessment scale and other instruments, and that patients with advanced illness have a high burden that can be measured by the ESAS.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
patients are the experts in defining their own symptom burden and this definition can be used to guide symptom management.
symptom burden is a patient defined concept that should be assessed in all patients receiving palliative care.
patients with high burden are those who have a high symptom score on the ESAS, and that patients with any ESAS score ≥7 should be considered at high risk of burden.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the term symptom burden needs to be more clearly defined.

patients with advanced illness should be asked about symptom burden as part of routine care and that symptom scores on the ESAS can be used to identify patients who may be at risk for self-defined burden.
